Unpalatable - Tasty Gallos

By: Joy Summers | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Looking for a franchise opportunity. Not all is as it seems at Tasty Gallos.

Unique Selling Point:
Great Case studies with documents, visuals and voice notes of the man they accuse of misleading them

Summary:
When Covid hit hard several South Africans turned to the Franchise industry to see if they could find an alternative source of Income. Tasty Gallos is marketed as the perfect low cost franchise opportunity and for around R700 000 you can be set up in your own halal shop selling chicken burgers, shawarma’s, burritos etc.

Glenn Dixon, Aneli and Omar, and several others we have spoken to off the record, now say they were lied to, gaslit, and bullied, and after only a few months, they walked away to save their sanity and from descending further into penury.

They blame 22 year old Muhammed Gutta, son of wealthy Discount Cash and Carry Nasser Gutta who they say is a fraud, a bully, and a liar. Each case study has their own particular grievance but across the board there is a pattern emerging, and it appears that it doesn’t take long before the franchises close.



Further information:
Briefly our case studies and sources can prove that the forecasts he gives them are completely inaccurate; there are hidden undisclosed costs; he buys on their accounts for other stores; he used a stolen operations manual from Muchacho’s; he used a dead man’s signature on a non-compliant and dangerous electrical certificate; he has no fixed head office address and meets prospective franchisees at a store and when pressed for an address he refuses to give one. He makes them buy catering grade (watered down) sauces from a sister company in which he has a financial interest, at ridiculous prices. He doesn’t give them a proper system to manage their fixed costs so they have no idea what their cost prices are. Instead he makes them count chicken pieces and put them into a confusing excel spread sheet. In the case of the case study I am about to go and see – he took her car and house papers in lieu of a loan even though he is not a registered financial service provider.
The influencer Kefilwe Mabote announced very publicly she was going to buy a franchise and then she went silent on the matter and never did. We can ask her why. Good investigative story with visuals of the owner of tasty Gallows and his threatening voice notes
We interview the case studies, a lawyer who specializes in franchise law, FASA and confront the man at the centre of the storm.



Extra Budget Items:
we could well need security on one day and there will be an extra cost if we need to send in a PI to get undercover footage.

FINAL SCRIPT TASTY GALLO’S FOR TX SUNDAY 27th FEB 2022 Fact checked

Commentary One
Welcome to the world of Tasty Gallos –where the deals are as hot as the sauce on the burgers

Up sound advert

Tasty Gallo’s is the new kid on the chicken franchise block.

Up sound Glitzy advert

Starting at R500 000 you too could own a custom made store with trained staff, a lease negotiated for you, and monthly turnover north of a million rand. What’s not to like?

Bongani
This was your way to financial freedom?
Omar Karim
Correct this was a way to use my package wisely to make a business and a future for my family

Commentary Two
Omar Karim’s job became a casualty of Covid. Tasty Gallo’s looked like a juicy alternative, so he met with founder Mohammed Gutta- who is so confident he stars in his own adverts

Up sound advert
You are hot ...
Gutta
thank you I know

Bongani Bingwa
Muhammed Gutta himself, who was he? What was he like?
Omar
Very vibrant man, very energetic man, a big talker
Bongani
Impressive?
Omar
Impressive, lots of talk about his brand, his ability, he makes you feel very, very ,safe

Commentary Three
And it’s that feeling of safety that has led to ten franchisees that we know of, to hand over their life savings to Gutta, only to walk away deeply in debt a few months later. That is what happened here in Norwood and has been repeated nationwide in other stores

Bongani
Was he charming?
Omar
Very! Silver tongued is what I call it.


Commentary Four
There are currently 19 Tasty Gallo’s stores countrywide. It’s a member of the Franchise Association of South Africa and Gutta is on an expansion drive

Up sound Muhammed subtitles
Firstly its Gutta not Gupta

Commentary Five
Fred Makgato is CEO of FASA

Bongani
You have a code of ethics. What does it say?
Fred
What it says is that if you become a member, you have to abide by what we call fair business practices by being honest and by being fair. Meaning that you can't go out there and try to mislead or to defraud people.

Commentary Six
These locks and closed up shops around Gauteng tell a story of losses on every meal, hopelessly over stated turnover projections, and expensive leases negotiated by Tasty Gallos, the franchisees can’t afford.

Omar Karim
He promises you things he can’t deliver but too bad you only find that out after he signed the franchise agreement and the stores are in operation.

Commentary Seven
This table at a popular Fish restaurant in Eastgate is where the Karim’s signed their franchise agreement. Gutta charged them R1.9 million rand for two stores – one in Centurion another in Cape Town

Omar
There's a particular table there that he likes meeting all of his franchisees, which I thought was odd because Tasty gallows East Gate is just literally around the corner.

Commentary Eight
Prospective franchisees bought the spin that Eastgate was turning over big money

Glenn
He also told me that that it's such a profitable business that Eastgate is turning over a million rand a month.

Commentary nine
In September 2021, Glenn Dixon opened his Benoni store with his inheritance from his mother

Up Sound Glen
To many memories!

Commentary ten
It lasted only 60 days.

Link
So how tasty was this business? You couldn’t really expect to hit all the targets in the first month but within weeks it seemed things were going from bad to worse - the sums weren’t adding up; the projected profits were not attainable

Commentary Eleven
The Karim’s tried to get financial information to see how the brand is doing, but Tasty Gallos replied that “they had never heard anything like that request in all their years as restauranteurs

Bongani
If I look at what Omar and Aneli signed in terms of the franchise agreement. What were the red flags for you there?
Ian
The franchise agreement itself on the face of it actually complied with the law. The disclosure document didn't because a lot of the information required in the disclosure document was missing.

Commentary twelve
Ian Jacobsberg is a specialist franchise attorney. He says Gutta was obliged to provide financial information and the status of the stores in operation

Ian
All these things were missing from the disclosure document.

Commentary thirteen
A disclosure document is important information that the franchisor must provide the franchisee

Ian Jacobsberg
So the fact that they were not part of the disclosure document is a contravention of the Consumer Protection Act Regulations.

Commentary fourteen
Gutta would not defend his brand in an interview with me.
Up sound
Bongani Will you give us an interview?
Gutta
Sorry will you call me back a bit later

Commentary fifteen
Instead he sent a letter denying any allegations of dishonesty, immorality or illegality in their business dealings with franchisees. Gutta says he always provided honest views about projected turnover, and if franchisees have failed it's because they haven't adhered to Gallo's business model.

Bongani
Who did you think you were getting into business with?
Glen
A genuine businessman. You do a background check on him, he's the director of so many other different companies, he's got all these restaurants that he's open and run

Link
From what the franchisees say Mohammed Gutta was the ultimate salesman. He came with high achievements and projected the acumen of an experienced businessman. But when did he earn that track record? Turns out he was only 22!!!

Commentary sixteen
And yet Gutta told franchisees that he has years of experience as an entrepreneur with a track record of successfully managing his own restaurants. He says he started in textiles and clothing, soon developed skills in the cell phone and IT sectors, and has experience in the stock market with insights into various industries.

But he was only 21 when he met Omar and Aneli Karim!

Bongani
you're an older guy. Didn't you feel upset that you were taken in by this lighty?
Omar
Yes, I was. Actually, when I came to the realization, nothing was true. All of it was fabricated lies to make you hear what you want to hear.

Commentary seventeen
Gutta has a privileged background. He seems to identify with the Wolf of Wall street character and he calls himself WOLFIE on snapchat. A company search suggests he sees himself as an ADONIS building an empire. But while Wolfie was empire building, Omar and Glen were watching their dreams crumble – and paying Tasty Gallo’s way too much for bottles of sauce

Glen
Well, it would have worked out to R832 if you only needed the one bottle of sauce from our franchisor

Commentary eighteen
Glen, previously an ops manager in a sauce factory began to question Gutta on why he was charging R550 for a bottle with extra for delivery

Bongani
How much should it have been?
Glen
Well, everybody else is charging on average R160 rand. And that's a premium grade sauce. The sauces that we were expected to use were cater grade sauces that were so watered down.

Commentary nineteen
Then another uncomfortable discovery, this time inside Tasty Gallo’s own instructions to franchisees. In several places as you can see here – Tasty Gallo’s appears to have cut and paste the operations manual from Mochachos- an established franchise and their competitor

Bongani
What did you think at that point?
Omar
I was shocked and appalled. I felt that holy smokes! I just way wasted my money. All of my money's gone on something that's not real!

Commentary twenty
But Gutta rejects any allegations of plagiarism and says if there are similarities to other operations manuals, then those similarities are purely coincidental.

Omar
And I said, things are not above-board here. There's even stock pictures that they used from the internet to imitate our food, which looks nothing like our food

Commentary twenty- one
For your upfront payment, Tasty Gallos gives you a complete shop fitted store including electrification. But load shedding led Glen to another revelation, when he tried to connect a generator

Glen
Only to have three independent electricians come around and tell me that we cannot connect this generator- we should never have been issued a certificate of compliance

Commentary twenty- two
Gutta refused to budge when confronted, so Glen reported him to the Electrical Contractors Association. The same day Muhammed Gutta cancelled Glen’s franchise

Glen
And I spoke to the director over there, and they confirmed with me that the person who actually issued that certificate had passed away the previous year in August
Bongani
No!
Glen
Yes!
Bongani
So you might have had worries until then, but at that point, there was no longer any doubt
Glen
There was no doubt whatsoever.

Commentary twenty three
Omar suspects the electricians signature may have been forged

Omar
And I was charged for this electrician, to fly over to Cape Town, to go and do the electrical work
Bongani laughs
You paid for a dead man to fly and do a certificate of compliance when he was already dead?
Omar
Correct. And you know what? He came in August again and he did my other store!

Link
So is this a credible business or just a chicken swindle? No franchisor can succeed if the franchisees are failing - so as many Tasty Gallows began to fold, it appears the only person scoring is Muhammad Gutta.

Commentary Twenty-four
Gutta tells Carte Blanche “we have a vested interest in ensuring that our franchisees succeed as their success is our success” But how true is that? Gutta has 19 stores currently open according to his website but we know of eleven others that have either closed since 2020 or been taken over by Gutta himself

Bongani
That's a significant number, isn't it?
Ian
Yeah, that is. Definitely, if you'd ask me and I'd known that it was. That is an unacceptable number.

Twenty -five
So is this a case where Gutta gets the upfront fee that is now close to a million rand a store, fits it out at a minimum cost and then takes them over for himself when the franchisees inevitably fail?

Bongani There seems to be a model here where franchises are snapped up for large sums of money and within a few months the thing folds. The franchisors takes over that franchise and sells it on to the next unsuspecting investor



Fred
That, for me, is a big worry. That's the reason we ended up having a clause in the Consumer Protection Act to prevent unfair business practices and try by all means to avoid

Commentary twenty six
Last year there was a store here in Lyttleton. Gutta took the franchisee’s house title deeds to make up her deposit. The store closed. In Benoni this store closed a few weeks ago- the franchisee too traumatised to speak to Carte blanche, But is in regular contact with Glen

Glen
She's she had to pledge her car to Muhammad because she fell short on money, knowing full well that she's got sickly children. He doesn't mind. He'll take it.

Bongani: What have you lost in all of this?
Glen
Everything. My entire inheritance is gone. And we are trying to survive. That's what we do.
Omar
Well, it's left us basically without businesses. And now we're going to have to pick up the pieces and move forward from this.

Commentary Twenty seven
FASA has now received an official complaint, they say they will begin investigations. Gutta meanwhile plans to expand to 40 stores and he claims there are many successful franchisees.

Hi Welcome to Tasty Gallos! 12 03

THE END

PROMO ONE 11 seconds
A group of hopeful franchisees have lost their life savings on a new Franchise chain that has big expansion plans
Omar
Well, it's left us basically without businesses.

PROMO TWO 21 seconds
A new chicken chain is on an expansion drive. But can it deliver on its promises
Bongani
Was he charming?
Omar
Very! Silver tongued is what I call it.

Commentary
But is this a legitimate business?
Bongani
Didn't you feel upset that you were taken in by this lighty?
Omar
Yes, I was. Actually, when I came to the realization, nothing was true.


PROMO THREE 21 seconds

Commentary
Franchisees who have sunk their savings into a new chicken franchise are left with a bitter taste in their mouths

Bongani
Who did you think you were getting into business with?
Glen
A genuine businessman. You do a background check on him, he's the director of so many other different companies, he's got all these restaurants that he's open and run

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Looking for a franchise opportunity. Not all is as it seems at Tasty Gallos.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Great Case studies with documents, visuals and voice notes of the man they accuse of misleading them
metadata.Summary: When Covid hit hard several South Africans turned to the Franchise industry to see if they could find an alternative source of Income. Tasty Gallos is marketed as the perfect low cost franchise opportunity and for around R700 000 you can be set up in your own halal shop selling chicken burgers, shawarma’s, burritos etc. Glenn Dixon, Aneli and Omar, and several others we have spoken to off the record, now say they were lied to, gaslit, and bullied, and after only a few months, they walked away to save their sanity and from descending further into penury. They blame 22 year old Muhammed Gutta, son of wealthy Discount Cash and Carry Nasser Gutta who they say is a fraud, a bully, and a liar. Each case study has their own particular grievance but across the board there is a pattern emerging, and it appears that it doesn’t take long before the franchises close.
metadata.Further information: Briefly our case studies and sources can prove that the forecasts he gives them are completely inaccurate; there are hidden undisclosed costs; he buys on their accounts for other stores; he used a stolen operations manual from Muchacho’s; he used a dead man’s signature on a non-compliant and dangerous electrical certificate; he has no fixed head office address and meets prospective franchisees at a store and when pressed for an address he refuses to give one. He makes them buy catering grade (watered down) sauces from a sister company in which he has a financial interest, at ridiculous prices. He doesn’t give them a proper system to manage their fixed costs so they have no idea what their cost prices are. Instead he makes them count chicken pieces and put them into a confusing excel spread sheet. In the case of the case study I am about to go and see – he took her car and house papers in lieu of a loan even though he is not a registered financial service provider. The influencer Kefilwe Mabote announced very publicly she was going to buy a franchise and then she went silent on the matter and never did. We can ask her why. Good investigative story with visuals of the owner of tasty Gallows and his threatening voice notes We interview the case studies, a lawyer who specializes in franchise law, FASA and confront the man at the centre of the storm.
